title: ICE cotton jumps amid tight stocks, weaker dollar
content:
ICE cotton's December 2026 contract settled at 88.35 cents, up 2.94 cents, after breaking above the May high and setting a fresh contract high. 
Volume rose to 71,522 contracts and open interest hit 361,871, signalling new participation behind the rally. 
Tight world stocks, Texas weather risks, strong Chinese reserve buying and a weaker US dollar supported momentum.

title: Indonesia’s textile industry eyes stronger growth amid recovery
content:
Indonesia’s textile and garment industry is showing signs of recovery, supported by rising investment, exports and improving industrial confidence. 
The sector exported $4.85 billion in the first half of 2026 and employs more than 3.8 million workers. 
The government is backing investment, restructuring, export financing, trade safeguards and green manufacturing to strengthen global competitiveness.

title: UK's GDP projected to grow 1.1% in 2026, 1.2% in 2027
content:
UK GDP growth is forecast at 1.1 per cent in 2026 and 1.2 per cent in 2027, according to HM Treasury’s August forecasts.
CPI inflation is projected at 3.4 per cent in Q4 2026 before easing to 2.2 per cent in Q4 2027.
Unemployment is expected at 5.2 per cent and 5.1 per cent respectively, while current account and public borrowing pressures remain elevated.

title: What factors are lifting cotton prices in Brazil?
content:
Brazilian cotton prices rose in early August as higher international prices and firm sellers pushed domestic values closer to export parity. 
The CEPEA/ESALQ Index increased 0.31 per cent to BRL 4.2171 per pound on August 17. 
Brazil’s July exports fell 29 per cent month on month but rose 22 per cent year on year, while global 2026/27 demand is forecast to exceed supply by 4.55 per cent.

title: 39% gone; yet fast fashion still can’t quit China
content:
TexPro shows US core-garment imports from China fell 41.4 per cent to $2.73 billion in January–May 2026, a loss of about $1.93 billion.
China’s share dropped to 9.5 per cent; Vietnam gained only about $47 million, Cambodia $203 million and Indonesia $96 million.
Buyers are splitting risk, but China’s fabric, trims, labour and logistics ecosystem remains hard to reproduce for ultra-fast fashion.

title: Italy defies decline in Hong Kong apparel imports on luxury demand
content:
Hong Kong’s apparel imports fell 2.6 per cent year on year to $2.959 billion in January-June 2026, TexPro data shows. 
Imports from Italy rose 2.8 per cent to $717.820 million, lifting its share to 24.25 per cent as demand for premium and luxury clothing stayed resilient. 
China remained the largest supplier at $1.238 billion, while Vietnam rose 6.9 per cent and France surged 28.0 per cent.

title: Bangladesh’s EU Apparel trade is entering a new competitive cycle
content:
Bangladesh is 97 days from scheduled LDC graduation, while a UN panel has recommended extending the date to 2029.
EU EBA preferences continue for three years after graduation, before clothing tariffs of roughly 9.6 to 12 per cent apply.
TexPro data show EU27 apparel imports from Bangladesh fell 7.43 per cent to $12.19 billion in January-May 2026, cutting its share to 28.95 per cent.

title: What helped Finland's Amer Sports beat guidance in Q2?
content:
Amer Sports, the US-based premium sports and outdoor group, delivered robust second-quarter FY26 results with revenue up 32 per cent YoY to $1.63 billion, outpacing guidance and driven by strong growth across all segments and regions. 
Net income attributable to equity holders soared 489 per cent to $107 million, while adjusted operating margin expanded to 12.8 per cent.

title: US apparel imports drop $3 bn—so where are the factory jobs?
content:
US apparel prices rose 3.9 per cent year on year in July, while apparel-manufacturing employment fell 9.1 per cent to 71,800.
TexPro says HS61-62 imports dropped 9.1 per cent to $30.25 billion in January-May 2026, with China losing $2.20 billion.
ASEAN-10 suppliers gained share as Vietnam, Cambodia and Indonesia grew; rerouting is more visible than reshoring.

title: UK apparel’s $242 mn gap is widening. What happens next?
content:
UK apparel imports reached $8.16 billion in January-May 2026, up 1.7 per cent, with Bangladesh at $1.94 billion and China at $1.70 billion.
Bangladesh’s lead widened to $242.1 million from $34.6 million a year earlier, while Vietnam and Cambodia also rose.
The UK rejected a simplified tariff schedule and confirmed a low-value import fee, making origin and classification more important.
